Optimise an RTMB object from several starting values

multistart.Rd

Latent Markov models often have several local optima of the likelihood. multistart() optimises obj from several starting values: the first is obj$par (the initial parameters), the others are random perturbations of it on the working scale. Afterwards, lama(obj) builds the model from the best fit, as RTMB keeps the parameters with the lowest negative log-likelihood it evaluated.

Usage

multistart(
  obj,
  nstarts = 20,
  sd = 1,
  starts = NULL,
  scale = c("fixed", "unit_info"),
  stop = c("bayes", "hits", "none"),
  hits = 3,
  sd_max = 2,
  tol = 1e-06,
  seed = NULL,
  optimizer = stats::nlminb,
  silent = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

obj

RTMB object from MakeADFun()

nstarts

maximum number of starts, including obj$par

sd

standard deviation of the perturbations on the working scale: a number, a vector of the length of obj$par, or a named list with one value per parameter (names as in the parameter list)

starts

optional matrix of starting values, one per row, with columns as obj$par; then nstarts and sd are ignored

scale

"fixed" for perturbations of obj$par with sd, or "unit_info" for perturbations of the first fit scaled by the unit information, see ‘Details’

stop

stopping rule: "bayes" (not used for given starts), "hits" or "none", see ‘Details’

hits

number of times the best optimum needs to be reached for stop = "hits"

sd_max

largest standard deviation for scale = "unit_info"

tol

relative tolerance for two runs to reach the same optimum

seed

optional seed for the random number generator

optimizer

optimisation function called as optimizer(par, fn, gr, ...), returning par and objective (like nlminb) or value (like optim)

silent

logical; if TRUE, nothing is printed

...

further arguments passed to optimizer

Value

output of optimizer for the best run, with two more elements: runs, a data frame with the negative log-likelihood nll, convergence code and maximum gradient component mgc of each run, and starts, the matrix of starting values used.

Details

Scatter. With scale = "fixed", the starts are obj$par plus normal noise with standard deviation sd. As most working parameters are on log or logit scale, sd = 1 is a relative change, so one value usually fits all parameters. Parameters on identity scale (e.g. means of normal distributions) may need their own sd, given as a named list like list(eta = 1, mu = 5).

With scale = "unit_info", the first fit is used to scale the others: they are drawn around it from a normal distribution with covariance \(n H^{-1}\), where \(H\) is the Hessian of the negative log-likelihood and \(n\) the number of observations. This is the information of a single observation (unit information), which does not shrink with \(n\) and takes correlations of the parameters into account. Standard deviations are capped at sd_max, for weakly identified parameters. If the Hessian is not positive definite (or allprobs is not reported, so \(n\) is unknown), the fixed sd is used instead.

Stopping. Two runs reach the same optimum if their negative log-likelihoods differ by less than tol (relative), so permuted states (label switching) count as the same optimum. Only converged runs (convergence code 0 and maximum gradient component below 0.01) count for stopping. With stop = "bayes", the Bayesian stopping rule of Boender and Rinnooy Kan (1987) is used: after \(k\) runs with \(w\) distinct optima, the expected number of optima is \(w(k-1)/(k-w-2)\), and multistart() stops when this is below \(w + 0.5\), i.e. probably no optimum is missed. The rule assumes that the starts are independent draws from one distribution, in which each optimum has an unknown probability of being reached (the probability mass of its basin of attraction), with a uniform prior on these probabilities. Hence, only the random starts count, not the first run from obj$par, and the rule is not used for given starts. It needs at least 8 converged random starts. "No optimum missed" is relative to the distribution of the starts: optima far away from it, or with a small basin of attraction, can be missed. With stop = "hits", it stops once the best optimum was reached hits times. In any case, at most nstarts starts are run.

References

Boender, C. G. E., & Rinnooy Kan, A. H. G. (1987). Bayesian stopping rules for multistart global optimization methods. Mathematical Programming, 37(1), 59-80.

Examples

nll <- function(par) {
  getAll(par, dat)
  Gamma <- tpm(eta)
  mu <- exp(log_mu); REPORT(mu)
  allprobs <- cbind(dgamma2(step, mu[1], exp(log_sigma[1])), dgamma2(step, mu[2], exp(log_sigma[2])))
  -forward(stationary(Gamma), Gamma, allprobs)
}
dat <- list(step = trex$step[1:500])
par <- list(eta = c(-2, -2), log_mu = log(c(0.3, 2.5)), log_sigma = log(c(0.2, 1.5)))
obj <- MakeADFun(nll, par, silent = TRUE)

opt <- multistart(obj, seed = 1)
#> start 1 - nll: 536.2127

#> start 10 - nll: 536.2127 
#> 10 starts, 9 converged, 1 distinct optima, best reached 9 times; stopped: Bayesian stopping rule 
opt$runs

#> 1  536.2127           0 1.657454e-04

#> 9  536.2127           0 2.866950e-03
#> 10 536.2127           0 3.189349e-05
mod <- lama(obj) # best fit

# starts scaled by the first fit
opt <- multistart(obj, scale = "unit_info", seed = 1)
